sketches.title: Permission Slip Catastrophe
sketches.premise: The school trip has gone gloriously wrong, and the permission slip is being rewritten one line at a time. Add the next true detail before the paper reaches the head teacher; make it more embarrassing for your partner if you can. The host announces each addition like a fresh scandal.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one line to the same permission slip and fits every fact already written; a skipped link jumps over a needed event, an ending declares the slip finished, and an undo removes or reverses a line already accepted.
sketches.move_shape: Add one new line to the slip, such as: “The coach driver has just phoned the head teacher to report that we are lost.” It must follow what stands, not quietly replace it.
sketches.first_card: The bus has stopped outside a closed theme park, with thirty pupils, two teachers, and one suspiciously warm suitcase.

sketches.title: Museum Audio Guide: The Incident
sketches.premise: You are recording a dramatic audio guide about the school trip that went off the rails. Take turns adding exactly one next beat to the same unfolding incident, while giving your partner the most ridiculous blame you can make fit. The host speaks as though civilisation itself is hanging on this recording.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it supplies the next single beat in the shared incident and preserves the whole transcript; a skipped link leaps past a required beat, an ending says what finally happened, and an undo cancels a recorded beat rather than adding one.
sketches.move_shape: Add one next beat, such as: “The class enters the gift shop, and the bell above the door starts shouting.” Do not add a second action or rewrite an earlier beat.
sketches.first_card: At the first museum stop, the guide opens a locked display case and finds the class mascot inside.

sketches.title: Lost-and-Found Quest
sketches.premise: The trip’s route, supplies, and dignity have vanished. Build one shared chain of clues, one step at a time, until the group can recover what was lost; make each clue useful but take a sly jab at your partner where the clue points. The host treats every tiny discovery as a heroic expedition, even when it is just a wet sock.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one clue or discovery that follows from all known clues; a skipped link makes an unexplained jump, an ending identifies the recovered item or final place, and an undo retracts a clue already found.
sketches.move_shape: Add one clue, such as: “The muddy footprint stops beneath the bench beside the vending machine.” It must narrow the search without solving the whole quest.
sketches.first_card: After lunch, the class discovers that the teacher’s master key, the map, and the emergency biscuits are missing.

sketches.title: Coach-Ride Dominoes
sketches.premise: One small mistake on the school coach has started a magnificent chain reaction. Add exactly the next consequence, keeping the same disaster alive while making your partner’s part in it as awkward as possible. The host narrates every wobble like a royal downfall.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds one immediate consequence caused by the latest situation and fits the complete chain; a skipped link jumps to a later result, an ending gives the final wreckage, and an undo erases or reverses a consequence already added.
sketches.move_shape: Add one consequence, such as: “Because the aisle is blocked, the science model slides into the driver’s lunch.” It must be the next result, not three disasters at once.
sketches.first_card: A pupil opens a fizzy drink just as the coach hits a speed bump, and the bottle points straight at the ceiling.

sketches.title: Field-Trip Courtroom
sketches.premise: The school trip has gone off the rails, and now the class must build one shared case about how it happened. Add one piece of evidence at a time; make it fit the record and make your partner look spectacularly guilty if you can. The host rules like a judge with a grudge and a very loud wig.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one new piece of evidence that follows from the whole case; a skipped link introduces evidence with no trail, an ending gives the verdict, and an undo withdraws evidence already entered.
sketches.move_shape: Add one exhibit or witness fact, such as: “Exhibit B is a receipt showing that the emergency taxi was paid for with the class fund.” It must strengthen the same case, not start a different one.
sketches.first_card: The class arrives at the castle with no teacher in sight, one broken gate, and a permission slip signed in glitter pen.

sketches.title: Return-Ticket Countdown
sketches.premise: The final train leaves soon, and the school trip is scattered across a place that clearly resents children. Build one shared rescue plan by adding exactly the next action; make your partner responsible for the most shameful job that still works. The host delivers each step as a grand military order, despite the missing socks and public panic.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one next action that is possible after everything already planned; a skipped link orders an action without its needed setup, an ending gets everyone safely home, and an undo cancels a planned action instead of advancing the plan.
sketches.move_shape: Add one next action, such as: “First, Morgan must distract the guard while Casey counts the pupils by the fountain.” It must be one step in the same plan, not a new rescue scheme.
sketches.first_card: The group is at a huge station, the return train leaves in twenty minutes, and the teacher has the tickets inside a locked museum locker.
